column4: Which attitude scales are used in social surveys? ‖ Bogardus's social distance scale, Thurstone's equal-appearing intervals, Likert's summated rating scale, Guttman's cumulative scale, and Guilford's work on rating.

सामाजिक सर्वेक्षणों में कौन-से अभिवृत्ति मापक प्रयोग होते हैं? ‖ बोगार्डस का सामाजिक दूरी मापक, थर्स्टन के समान-अंतराल, लिकर्ट का योग-आधारित श्रेणी मापक, गटमैन का संचयी मापक, और गिलफ़ोर्ड का श्रेणीकरण कार्य।

What are culture realms? ‖ Large world regions sharing a broad culture: Russell and Kniffen (1951) named 7 culture worlds; Spencer and Thomas gave 11 first-order realms and 50 second-order regions. From big to small: culture realm, culture region, culture area, culture trait.

What is ethnicity? ‖ A shared identity based on culture, language, religion, ancestry or homeland, chosen and felt by the group; unlike race it is cultural, not biological.
जातीयता क्या है? ‖ संस्कृति, भाषा, धर्म, वंश या मातृभूमि पर आधारित साझा पहचान, जिसे समूह चुनता और महसूस करता है; प्रजाति के विपरीत यह सांस्कृतिक है, जैविक नहीं।

Today biologists see human variation as continuous, so race is a weak biological idea. ¦ Who are the Andaman tribes? ‖ The Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa and Sentinelese are Negrito peoples, short and dark, among the oldest groups in Asia; the Nicobarese are Mongoloid.

प्रजातियों का वर्गीकरण कैसे हुआ है? ‖ प्रारंभिक योजनाओं ने दिखने वाले लक्षण प्रयोग किए: क्यूवियर (1817) ने त्वचा का रंग; ग्रिफ़िथ टेलर ने प्रवास कटिबंध; सामान्य समूह कॉकेशॉयड, मंगोलॉयड और नीग्रॉयड थे। आज जीवविज्ञानी मानव विविधता को सतत मानते हैं, इसलिए प्रजाति एक कमज़ोर जैविक विचार है। ¦ अंडमान की जनजातियाँ कौन हैं? ‖ ग्रेट अंडमानी, ओंगे, जारवा और सेंटिनली नीग्रिटो लोग हैं, छोटे कद और गहरे रंग के, एशिया के सबसे पुराने समूहों में; निकोबारी मंगोलॉयड हैं।

Which traditional peoples are often asked? ‖ The Inuit of Arctic Canada and Greenland, the Yukaghir of Siberia, the Batwa (pygmies) of the Congo forest, the Bedouin such as the Rwala of the Arabian deserts, the Maasai of East Africa and the San of the Kalahari.

What is welfare geography? ‖ David M. Smith's approach (1970s): who gets what, where and how; it maps spatial variation in well-being and inequality using social indicators, which grew in the USA in the 1960s. ¦ What does social geography study? ‖ How society is organised over space: social groups, their patterns of living, well-being and inequality, and the spaces of class, caste, ethnicity and gender; David M. Smith's work (1973) began welfare geography.

How should tribes be treated? ‖ Verrier Elwin argued for isolation in 'national parks', G. S. Ghurye for assimilation, and Nehru's tribal Panchsheel for integration with respect for tribal ways.

Guha found all major strains in India. ¦ How have races been classified? ‖ Early schemes used visible traits: Cuvier (1817) used skin colour; Griffith Taylor used migration zones; common groups were Caucasoid, Mongoloid and Negroid. Today biologists see human variation as continuous, so race is a weak biological idea. ¦ Who are the Andaman tribes? ‖ The Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa and Sentinelese are Negrito peoples, short and dark, among the oldest groups in Asia; the Nicobarese are Mongoloid.
